title: Smooth-atlas Cech spectral sequence for big etale module direct images
statement: Work in the universes and small-skeleton convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. For a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme] and an algebraic stack $\mathcal Z/S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], its big etale site has all objects and arrows of the fibred category in [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], with coverings lying over jointly surjective etale scheme maps. Its structure sheaf is $\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z}(z)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ for $z$ over $U$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $h:\mathcal A\to\mathcal Z$, direct image has value $(h_*N)(z)=\Gamma(\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal Z}U,N|_{\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal Z}U})$; restrictions are induced by base change, and pullback of a module along a stack morphism means precomposition. Higher direct images are computed by injective resolutions in all module sheaves [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ and $u:\mathcal U\to\mathcal X$ be morphisms of algebraic stacks over $S$. Assume $u$ is representable by algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and surjective, meaning field-extension-local lifting of every field-valued object. For $p\geq0$ form $\mathcal U_p=\mathcal U\times_{\mathcal X}\cdots\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal U$ with $p+1$ factors and augmentation $u_p:\mathcal U_p\to\mathcal X$, using [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. For every module sheaf $F$ on $\mathcal X$, there is a natural first-quadrant cohomological spectral sequence [def-sp-spectral-sequence] in the big etale module category of $\mathcal Y$ $$E_1^{p,q}=R^q(f\circ u_p)_*(u_p^*F)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad R^{p+q}f_*F,\qquad p,q\geq0.$$ Its first differential is the alternating sum of face restriction maps. The differentials have bidegree $(r,1-r)$; every entry eventually stabilizes to $E_\infty^{p,q}$. For every $n\geq0$, the abutment has a finite filtration $R^nf_*F=F^0\supseteq F^1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq F^{n+1}=0$ with $F^p/F^{p+1}\cong E_\infty^{p,n-p}$. There is no quasi-coherence, qcqs, Noetherian or finite-type assumption on $F$ or $f$.

proof.text: Since $u$ is representable, its smoothness after every scheme base change is the smooth-chart smoothness of [lem-sfb-stack-smooth-presentation-criterion], and its surjectivity is the field-extension lifting used there. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-stack-family-etale-object-lifts] to the singleton family $u$. It gives, for every object $x$ of $\mathcal X$, a jointly surjective etale covering $\{x_i\to x\}$ with $x_i\cong u(z_i)$. All covering schemes and objects remain in the fixed site universe, including the empty test scheme. This verifies the local-image hypothesis of [lem-sfb-stack-relative-cech-module-augmentation-exact].

The module category on the chosen small ringed site is Grothendieck abelian by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], hence has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Successively embed $F$ and the cokernels of the preceding embeddings into injectives, obtaining $0\to F\to I^0\to I^1\to\cdots$, and set $I^q=0$ for $q<0$. This is the resolution of [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Each $u_p$ is representable: it is a composite of iterated $2$-base changes of $u$, and representability by algebraic spaces is preserved by $2$-base change and composition by [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus]. Each $\mathcal U_p$ is an algebraic stack by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products]. Thus [lem-sfb-stack-representable-module-injective-transport] makes $u_p^*$ exact and $u_p^*I^q$ injective, and makes $(u_p)_*u_p^*I^q$ injective. In particular $u_p^*I^\bullet$ resolves $u_p^*F$.

For each $q$, apply [lem-sfb-stack-relative-cech-module-augmentation-exact] to $I^q$, using step 1. Its exact augmented row has every term injective by step 2. This row is split exact: the inclusion of $I^q$ in its degree-zero term has a retraction by injectivity, so the cokernel is an injective direct summand; repeat with its inclusion in the next term. The resulting successive splittings give a contraction. Applying the additive functor $f_*$ preserves those splitting identities, hence yields the exact row
$$0\to f_*I^q\to(fu_0)_*u_0^*I^q\to(fu_1)_*u_1^*I^q\to\cdots.$$
Here $f_*(u_p)_*=(fu_p)_*$ is the canonical composition identification: both are right adjoint to the equal precomposition functor $(fu_p)^*=u_p^*f^*$ supplied by the transport node.

Put $C^{p,q}=(fu_p)_*u_p^*I^q$ for $p,q\geq0$, zero elsewhere. The horizontal differential is the alternating face restriction map $\delta$ and the vertical differential is induced by $d_I$. The cosimplicial identities pair the two orders of deleting distinct factors with opposite signs, so $\delta^2=0$; functoriality of restrictions gives $\delta d_I=d_I\delta$. These are the double-complex identities of [def-sp-double-complex-total]; its total differential is $\delta+(-1)^p d_I$. The restriction augmentation $f_*I^\bullet\to C^{0,\bullet}$ is a chain map killed by the horizontal differential. Step 3 verifies the rowwise quasi-isomorphism hypothesis of [lem-sc-first-quadrant-column-augmentation]. It gives a quasi-isomorphism $f_*I^\bullet\to\operatorname{Tot}C$, hence $H^n(\operatorname{Tot}C)\cong R^nf_*F$ by the definition of higher direct image on this resolution.

Apply the first spectral sequence (I) of [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] to $C$. Its first page is
$$E_1^{p,q}=H^q(C^{p,\bullet})=R^q(fu_p)_*(u_p^*F),$$
since step 2 supplies the injective resolution used by this derived functor. Its $d_1$ is induced by $\delta$, hence is the alternating face restriction map. The same theorem gives differentials of bidegree $(r,1-r)$, entrywise stabilization and a finite filtration of $H^n(\operatorname{Tot}C)$, with successive quotients $E_\infty^{p,n-p}$. Carry the filtration across step 4's cohomology isomorphism: its endpoints are $F^0=R^nf_*F$ and $F^{n+1}=0$, and it has exactly the required quotients. Only $0\leq p\leq n$ occurs in total degree $n$; no cohomological dimension bound or geometric finiteness assumption enters.

For a map $F\to F'$, [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists] supplies a cochain lift $I\to I'$ commuting with the augmentations. Functoriality of precomposition, direct image and face restriction makes it a map of the augmented double complexes above; [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] gives its map on pages and filtrations. Two lifts are homotopic by [lem-weil-pbc-lift-to-injective-unique-up-to-homotopy], applied to the resolution $F[0]\to I$ and the two maps into $I'$. Applying $(fu_p)_*u_p^*$ to that homotopy gives column homotopies, which commute with all face restrictions. Thus the maps agree on column cohomology, hence on $E_1$ and every later page. The total homotopy is $(-1)^p h$ on column $p$: the horizontal terms cancel and the vertical terms give the difference of the two total maps. It preserves the column filtration. Consequently the induced abutment map is the usual $R^nf_*$ map and is independent of the lift. Applying this also to identity maps between two choices of resolution proves independence of that choice; compositions agree by the same argument. This establishes naturality in module sheaf $F$.
